facts.statement: The genus was described from a skull found in the Arcadia Park Shale at Cedar Hill in Dallas County, Texas.
facts.quote: The genus was described from a skull discovered in an exposure of the Arcadia Park Shale (lower Middle Turonian) at Cedar Hill, Dallas County in the south-central part of the DFW Metroplex in Texas, United States.

facts.statement: The type specimen, skull SMU 73056, was discovered in 1992 by a member of the Dallas Paleontological Society and donated to the Shuler Museum of Paleontology.
facts.quote: The skull (SMU 73056, Shuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University) was found in 1992 by a member of the Dallas Paleontological Society, who then donated to the museum.

facts.statement: Fragmentary specimens of Russellosaurus have been recovered from the Kamp Ranch Limestone at two other localities in the Dallas area.
facts.quote: Other fragmentary specimens of Russellosaurus have been recovered from the slightly older Kamp Ranch Limestone at two other localities in the Dallas area.

facts.statement: Russellosaurus is the second mosasaur species named after Dale A. Russell, following Selmasaurus russelli.
facts.quote: This is the second species of mosasaur to have been named for Russell, the first being Selmasaurus russelli (Wright and Shannon, 1988).

facts.statement: The type specimen of Russellosaurus is notable as the oldest well-preserved mosasaur found in North America.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Russellosaurus is notable as being the oldest well-preserved mosasaur yet found in North America.

facts.statement: The skull of Russellosaurus possesses sixteen maxillary teeth and sixteen dentary teeth.
facts.quote: Sixteen maxillary teeth and 16 dentary teeth.

facts.statement: The anterior premaxilla of Russellosaurus is broad and blunt, with an oblique premaxillary-maxillary suture when viewed from above.
facts.quote: Anterior premaxilla broad and blunt, in dorsal view the premaxillary-maxillary suture is oblique.

facts.statement: The frontal bone of Russellosaurus shows incipient emargination caused by the external nares.
facts.quote: Incipient emargination of the frontal by the external nares.

facts.statement: The pineal foramen is located in the center of the triangular parietal table in Russellosaurus.
facts.quote: The pineal foramen is located in the centre of the triangular parietal table.

facts.statement: Russellosaurus is a small mosasauroid with a light build and a narrow frontal bone with a length-to-width ratio of 1.6:1.
facts.quote: Mosasáurido pequeño, de constitución ligera, con un frontal estrecho con una proporción de longitud-anchura de 1.6:1.

facts.statement: Russellosaurus was designated the type genus of the new parafamily Russellosaurina (or subfamily Russellosaurinae).
facts.quote: Polcyn et Bell (2005, p. 322) designated Russellosaurus the type genus of a new parafamily of mosasaurs, the Russellosaurina (= subfamily Russellosaurinae of Bell, 1997).

facts.statement: The clade Russellosaurina includes mosasaurs more closely related to Tylosaurinae and Plioplatecarpinae than to Mosasaurinae, with Tethysaurus, Yaguarasaurus, and Russellosaurus forming its sister group.
facts.quote: This clade of marine lizards is defined as all mosasaurs more closely related to the subfamilies Tylosaurinae and Plioplatecarpinae and their sister group, consisting of the taxa Tethysaurus, Yaguarasaurus, and Russellosaurus, their common ancestor and all descendants than to the subfamily Mosasaurinae.

facts.statement: The skull of Russellosaurus displays many diagnostic characters of Plioplatecarpinae while retaining many primitive traits.
facts.quote: The skull of Russelosaurus shows many characters diagnostic of the Plioplatecarpinae while retaining many plesiomorphic traits.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Russellosaurus coheni is believed to belong to a subadult individual based on the lack of basicranial fusion and high bone vascularization suggesting rapid growth.
facts.quote: Based on the lack of fusion between elements of the basicranium and a high degree of vascularization of the bone surface, which suggests the animal was undergoing a rapid growth stage when it died, the holotype skull of Russellosaurus coheni is believed to have come from a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Russellosaurus fossils were found in the Arcadia Park Shale at Cedar Hill, Texas, dating to the early middle Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Este género fue descrito con base en un cráneo descubierto en rocas expuestas de la Pizarra Arcadia Park (a inicios de la mitad de la etapa del Turoniense) en Cedar Hill, en el condado de Dallas en el centro-sur de Texas, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The genus Russellosaurus was named by Polcyn and Bell in 2005.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Russellosaurus (genus), Polcyn and Bell 2005

facts.statement: Russellosaurus belongs to the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Yaguarasaurinae

facts.statement: This animal is classified within the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Russellosaurus lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Russellosaurus has been recorded in the database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
